extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of natural philosophy / sociology (educated general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Describe and evaluate the principles by which like units/groupings separate and integrate (segregation) and the processes by which motions dissipate and systems approach balance (equilibration) across physical, biological, and social domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory segregation and idea-formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Like groups of forces passing through organs of sense and percipient centres become segregated (separated from unlike groups), and each such segregated series constitutes a state of consciousness we call our idea of the genus or species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains that as mixed forces pass through sensory organs they are separated into like groups; structural changes in the organism represent the integrated series of motions that produced them. This is offered as the mechanistic basis for how ideas (genus/species) arise from sensory segregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural consolidation by repetition (frequency → readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two phenomena experienced in a given order are repeated in the same order, the nerves previously affected are again affected and the molecular modification they received is increased; such modifications involve a diminution of resistance to subsequent motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that mental connexion and the classification of relations increase with repetition; readiness (ease of future discharge) is 'proportionate to the frequency with which experience repeats the connexion of phenomena.' The text ties classification of relations to the same process as classification of things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification develops pari passu with impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The connexions of co-existence and sequence among impressions become sorted into kinds and grouped simultaneously with the impressions themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author emphasizes that relations (order/sequence) are segregated along with sensations; thus classification of relations occurs alongside sensory classification. This is used to explain associative memory and concept formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical conditions as causes of social segregation
rubrics_metrics.description: External physical forces (climate, food, other physical conditions) act to expel or maintain peoples of certain bodily constitutions in particular localities, thereby effecting and maintaining segregations of mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: northern races in tropical regions cannot permanently exist; maintenance of populations in difficult climates requires continuous immigration/emigration. Physical conditions are primary incident forces producing segregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental affinities and desire for similarity produce social grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Men display affinities for others like themselves; emigrants desire to get back among their own people, and where restrained they often form colonies—small societies of their own—showing a tendency to re-unite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is given as a mutual-polarity force: desires move people along lines of least resistance toward social units where their feelings get satisfaction (sympathy and adapted social conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Segregation via education and occupational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Education (in its widest sense) and training mould citizens to special functions, producing likenesses that lead to class-segregations and occupational aggregation (e.g., operative builders unions, medical associations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those trained for bodily labour become more like each other in powers of action; those trained for brain-work acquire other common characters. Where occupations favor aggregation, specially assimilated citizens concentrate in localities or form associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation where occupation meets least resistance (economic localisation principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a locality renders a certain kind of industrial action less resistive (less total labour/expenditure), social units moulded to that occupation will move toward and concentrate there (example: Glasgow and iron-ship building).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author frames this as an instance of the general law of direction of motion: individuals pursue courses of least resistance; places that lower the 'total labour required' attract and concentrate practitioners, or cause immigration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple likeness-types cause overlapping segregations (source of anomalies)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are likenesses of disposition, taste, intellectual culture, class-training, political feeling, etc.; different species of likeness lead to different segregative processes which traverse and sometimes antagonize one another, causing incomplete integrations and observed anomalies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns that apparent anomalies (exceptions to the general law) are often due to intersecting kinds of likeness and indirect antagonisms among segregative processes; analysis should account for multiple likeness dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four abstract propositions linking units, forces, and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: First: like units, subject to a uniform force, will be moved alike. Second: like units under unlike forces will be differently moved. Third: unlike units under uniform force will be differently moved. Fourth: incident forces themselves are analogously affected (like forces on like units modified similarly; unlike forces on like units modified dissimilarly; like forces on unlike units dissimilarly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These propositions are presented as reductions of the general principle that unlikeness in either factor (force or matter) necessitates unlikeness in effects; they are explicitly tied to the doctrine of the persistence of force and are used to deduce segregation phenomena across domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary from persistence of force: unlikeness ↔ unlikeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Any unlikeness in incident forces where the things acted on are alike must generate a difference in effects, and vice versa; conversely, if both forces and things are alike, effects must be alike—otherwise persistence of force is violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This logical corollary is used to infer that redistributions and segregations observed in evolution are implications of the persistence of force; it is the philosophical grounding for the earlier abstract propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibration by decomposition and dissipation of motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions are continually decomposed into divergent and re-divergent motions; by continuance they are reduced to insensible motions and ultimately to quiescence—the universal progress toward equilibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: rolling stones transferring momentum until rest; water flowing to lowest level and being arrested; waves diminishing into atmospheric/shore motion; harp-string vibrations becoming aerial pulses and finally thermal undulations. The proximate rationale is multiplication of effects and progressive division of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three empirical truths about equilibration in aggregates
rubrics_metrics.description: First: the various motions of an aggregate are separately equilibrated—the smallest or those meeting greatest resistance disappear first. Second: when parts move with little external resistance, a 'equilibrium mobile' (moving equilibrium) tends to be established. Third: this moving equilibrium eventually lapses into complete equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spinning-top example illustrates separate dissipation of subsidiary motions (horizontal translation and 'wabbling') leaving rotatory motion, and eventual transition to complete equilibrium. The text emphasizes component-wise equilibration and relative persistence of motions that meet less resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four orders of equilibration (typology)
rubrics_metrics.description: First order: simple transient motions (projectiles) decomposed quickly. Second order: vibrations/oscillations producing visible rhythm then lost to invisible rhythms. Third order: dependent moving equilibrium where incoming supply replaces dissipation (e.g., steam engine balancing fuel-supplied motion with expenditure). Fourth order: independent or perfect moving equilibrium (e.g., the Solar System with negligible resisting medium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author presents this typology to classify equilibrative phenomena; the third ('dependent moving equilibrium') is especially noted as commonly encountered in evolution, while the fourth describes nearly perfect long-term moving equilibria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization: equilibria are relative; centre-of-gravity loses motion while parts retain relative motion
rubrics_metrics.description: All equilibrations are relative rather than absolute: arrival at a moving equilibrium is the disappearance of some movement of the aggregate with respect to external points while constituent parts retain relative motions; conversely, absolute equilibria still have molecular/insensible relative motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reframes 'equilibrium mobile' as a case of the general equilibration process: e.g., in systems like the Solar System the mean state of the whole remains constant though parts move relative to each other. This is used to argue that evolution proceeds until a moving equilibrium is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution's endpoint: moving equilibrium with specialized structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The evolution of every aggregate proceeds until an equilibrium mobile is established; structurally, this corresponds to arrangements of forces that counterbalance all forces to which the aggregate is subject, and the limit of heterogeneity is formation of as many specializations and combinations of parts as there are specialized/combinations of forces to be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text asserts that residual forces must be eliminated by redistribution of matter and specialization; examples include stages in nebulous condensation (rings → planets) where each stage is a transitional moving equilibrium tending toward more complete equilibration.
